papers.title: ProlateNet: Sampling-rate transfer of convolutional networks with a weights-only certificate for physiological signals
papers.summary: Proposes ProlateNet, a convolutional architecture that builds kernels from prolate spheroidal wave functions to suppress aliasing and enable sampling-rate transfer, with a weights-only certificate of transfer error. Across fourteen first-layer designs on three public EEG/ECG datasets, it was the only design accurate and stable at all rates, with mean worst drop of at most 0.003 macro-F1 and a certificate ranking designs by measured transfer (Spearman ρ = 0.92).

papers.title: NED-Net: open-source software for building and refining seizure detectors during rodent EEG experiments
papers.summary: Introduces NED-Net, open-source software that trains and continuously retrains rodent seizure detectors using reviewed candidate events as labels. A detector across cohorts went from mostly-seizure detections with low per-animal recall to, after cohort-specific retraining, convulsive recall of 64% (up from 15%) with at least one reference seizure in every animal.

papers.title: When Should Deployed BCI Decoders Adapt? A Resource-Priced Ladder for Frozen EEG Trunks
papers.summary: Proposes a resource-priced adaptation ladder (factory -> conjugate Bayesian head -> affine map, with fine-tuning as escape hatch) outside a frozen EEG encoder, gated by a utility pricing accuracy, fit time, and label cost. A clean-referenced gate cut adaptation rate from 0.56 to 0.11 on field-like sessions, and a lightweight LDA head matched or exceeded frozen-trunk accuracy across five encoders at ~23x lower fit time, though no reliable head gain appeared under natural drift in two BNCI checks.

papers.title: LogicSleep: a neurosymbolic-guided framework for explainable and personalized sleep staging.
papers.summary: LogicSleep is a neurosymbolic framework combining a CNN-graph U-Net backbone with Conditional Random Fields and differentiable-logic transition rules to produce physiologically valid, subject-adaptive sleep staging. It outperformed strong baselines on ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3, including under cross-dataset settings, and improved sequence-level metrics and explainability.

papers.title: Adapting Tensor Kernel Machines to Enable Efficient Transfer Learning for Seizure Detection.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
papers.summary: Introduces Adapt-TKM, an adaptive tensor kernel machine that transfers knowledge from a source model via regularization while using low-rank tensor networks to avoid adding parameters. Applied to behind-the-ear EEG seizure detection, patient adaptation improved detection for most patients and significantly outperformed a fully patient-specific model with ~100x fewer parameters than adaptive SVM and faster inference.

papers.title: From real to synthetic: PSG-GAN learns sleep apnea signal dynamics for AI training
papers.summary: Develops PSG-GAN, a generative adversarial network that co-synthesizes longer multi-signal polysomnography segments capturing obstructive sleep apnea dynamics, including inter-signal interactions such as photoplethysmography-based heart rate changes around obstructions. A scoring model trained solely on synthetic signals reached good sleep staging (κ = 0.71 and 0.63) and respiratory event segmentation (κ = 0.57 and 0.60) on healthy and OSA test sets.

papers.title: Exploratory evaluation of electroencephalogram-derived features for classification of mild cognitive impairment in two independent datasets.
papers.summary: This exploratory study evaluated EEG-derived spectral, synchronization-likelihood, and graph-metric features for classifying mild cognitive impairment versus healthy controls in Japanese and Iranian datasets. Lower-alpha-band exponentially transformed features achieved nested cross-validated accuracies of 88.24% (Japanese) and 83.61% (Iranian), but bidirectional cross-dataset transfer dropped to 40.98% and 58.82%, indicating dataset-specific characteristics.

papers.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG sleep staging using a serpentine dataflow for long temporal convolutions (6.2× and 2.25× fewer memory accesses than output- and weight-stationary dataflows) and hybrid layer-wise dynamic quantization (4.16× model-size reduction). Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, it consumes 0.40 mW with 258× speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor, staying within 0.15% of floating-point 5-class accuracy and 0.51% for N3 sensitivity on MASS-SS3.

papers.title: EEGSync: Unitary Temporal Alignment Method for Naturalistic and Resting-State EEG
papers.summary: Introduces EEGSync, a complex-valued unitary Procrustes method that aligns band-limited analytic EEG signals by mapping subjects into a reference temporal coordinate system via economy-SVD, preserving pairwise relationships and channel power. In subject-independent cross-validation, EEGSync features reached AUROC 0.9600 and 89.45% accuracy for eyes-open versus eyes-closed discrimination, and AUROC 0.9272 for Alzheimer's disease versus healthy controls in eyes-closed recordings.

papers.title: Sample size critically shapes the reliability of EEG case-control findings in psychiatry.
papers.summary: Quantified how sample size affects reliability of resting-state EEG case-control comparisons using repeated random subsampling in a 2,874-participant multisite dataset spanning ADHD, autism spectrum disorder, anxiety, learning disorders, and controls. Small samples produced unstable, inflated, highly variable effect sizes, whereas larger samples converged on uniformly small but robust effects, with statistical power rising steeply and false positive rates remaining relatively stable.

papers.title: Rest-to-task transfer of sparse-to-full EEG reconstruction for cognitive-load decoding.
papers.summary: Evaluated a 4-to-21-channel convolutional sparse-to-full EEG reconstruction model trained only on resting-state data and transferred to N-back working-memory tasks in participants with major depressive disorder. Reconstruction partially preserved task-relevant spectral structure without fine-tuning, but the preferred electrode configuration was endpoint-dependent (EMOT best for waveform fidelity; CROSS best for spectral preservation and 2-back vs 0-back classification), and generic reconstruction fidelity did not correspond to preserved cognitive-task features.

papers.title: GALA: Gallery-Level Alignment for Real-Life Vision Decoding from EEG
papers.summary: Proposes incremental transductive calibration for EEG visual decoding, where a decoder is calibrated only on unlabeled accumulated EEG and a known candidate gallery, and introduces GALA, a label-free method combining shrinkage whitening, hubness correction, and Sinkhorn-Procrustes gallery alignment. On THINGS-EEG-2 with a 200-image gallery, GALA raised top-1 accuracy for a new subject from 28% to 67% over 53 minutes and was the most accurate label-free method across all 60 evaluation settings, averaging 6.6 points above the best competitor.

papers.title: EEG-based depression detection via temporal-frequency-dynamical feature fusion.
papers.summary: Develops a sorting-guided multi-domain feature coupling framework that fuses temporal, frequency, and nonlinear dynamical EEG features with an ordered coupling strategy for depression detection classified by standard machine learning. Evaluated on MODMA (major depressive disorder vs healthy controls) and EDRA (high- vs low-risk individuals), the framework reportedly outperformed comparison approaches.

papers.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
papers.summary: High-density EEG with spectral and complexity measures was used to characterize eight progressively deepening jhana absorption meditation states in 20 advanced meditators alongside phenomenological ratings. The states showed widespread posterior-central power reductions, posterior aperiodic flattening, and elevated entropy-based complexity that persisted into the most minimal states, dissociating neural complexity from experiential richness.

papers.title: Spider Pattern: An adaptive EEG feature extraction method for Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia classification.
papers.summary: Evaluates an adaptive time-domain Spider Pattern feature extraction method with Social Spider Algorithm feature selection and a feedforward neural network for Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and control classification in 88 participants. Nested leave-one-subject-out validation yielded subject-level accuracies of 78.46% (AD vs NC), 71.15% (FTD vs NC), and 52.54% (AD vs FTD), while segment-wise 10-fold results (up to 93%) were inflated by participant leakage; AD-vs-FTD discrimination was not reliable.

papers.title: Hybrid framework utilizing interval Type-2 fuzzy entropy and ScaleDual-CNN for differential diagnosis of dementia using rest-state EEG signals.
papers.summary: Proposes a hybrid framework using interval type-2 fuzzy entropy (IT2-FE) in alpha and theta bands with spectral, Hjorth, and connectivity features, combined with a ScaleDual-CNN and machine learning for differential diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia from resting-state EEG in 88 OpenNeuro subjects. IT2-FE identified 35 significant features versus 3 for spectral entropy and reached subject-independent AUCs of 0.96 (control), 0.93 (AD), and 0.89 (FTD), with epoch-level accuracy of 95.29%.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG features of cognitive fluctuations across the Lewy body disease spectrum.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 53 Lewy body disease patients, resting-state EEG features (dominant frequency, dominant frequency prevalence-alpha, individual alpha peak frequency) were significantly lower in those with cognitive fluctuations and predicted group membership after adjustment for age, sex, and MoCA (AUC 0.85-0.86). The authors propose these EEG features as a potential biomarker to improve diagnosis of Lewy body dementia.

papers.title: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
papers.summary: Analyzing EEG from 1,534 participants aged 5-21 during a contrast-change discrimination task, the study dissociated developmental components of perceptual decisions: accuracy improved via fewer attention lapses and more efficient evidence accumulation reaching half their change by about 9 years, whereas non-decision time shortened only between 11 and 14 years. Visual response strength did not grow with age, indicating accuracy and speed mature on separate timetables.

papers.title: Cross-modality Knowledge Transfer Between fMRI and EEG for Improved Single-modality Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis.
papers.summary: Proposes FE-KTNet, an fMRI-EEG knowledge transfer network that learns fused multi-scale spatiotemporal representations from paired data and distills them back to modality-specific models through cross-modality fusion and feature/logit alignment. Across 14 multicenter datasets (2,766 fMRI, 1,842 EEG subjects), it improved fMRI-only and EEG-only accuracy by 3.4%/6.1% for AD-NC, 5.2%/8.0% for MCI-NC, and 3.5%/7.1% for AD-MCI versus baselines.

papers.title: Shared-Encoder Residual Task-Bridging Network for Motor Execution to Motor Imagery EEG Transfer in Brain-Computer Interfaces
papers.summary: The authors propose SE-RTBNet, a shared-encoder residual task-bridge network with performance-aware routing for intra-subject cross-task transfer from motor execution to motor imagery EEG decoding. On three public datasets it achieved average classification accuracies of 69.39%, 74.61%, and 98.94%, outperforming existing transfer-learning algorithms and reducing reliance on MI calibration data.

papers.title: A multimodal dataset for the study of cybersickness under stress and mental workload during immersive VR driving.
papers.summary: Presents a multimodal dataset from 60 participants performing phase-based immersive VR driving tasks, with a final phase designed to elicit mental workload, stress, or both. Records EEG, cardiovascular, respiration, and head-movement data alongside self-report cybersickness, workload, and stress measures, and demonstrates changes in cybersickness symptoms across driving phases and conditions.

papers.title: Beyond sensitivity: Performance, methodological heterogeneity, and real-time translation of wrist-worn convulsive seizure detection devices - A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 studies (1598 participants, 71,310 monitoring hours) found pooled sensitivities of approximately 93% for convulsive and 96% for generalized tonic-clonic seizures, with a pooled false-alarm rate of ~0.39/24 h and mean detection latency of 30.04 s. Heterogeneity exceeded 75% and methodological variability was extensive, with only one study evaluating real-time caregiver notification and intervention.

papers.title: Cross-Attention Estimation of Asynchronous EEG Functional Networks for Affective Disorder Characterization.
papers.summary: Proposes an attention-based causal-discovery framework (CACD) for interpretable asynchronous EEG functional networks that jointly estimates directed influence strength, transmission delay, and modulation sign using a dual-branch decoder, learnable cross-attention mask, and attention-gradient consistency. CACD recovered causal structures and delays on nine benchmarks and achieved competitive subject-independent affective-disorder classification on three clinical EEG datasets, with delay and modulation adding discriminative value beyond directed influence.

papers.title: Preferential responses to spectrally degraded sentences in the human cortex revealed by intracranial electrophysiology.
papers.summary: Using intracranial EEG in neurosurgical epilepsy patients, this study characterized differential cortical responses to clear versus 3-band noise-vocoded sentences, finding sustained clear-preferred and less common vocoded-preferred event-related band power responses in core auditory cortex and the dorsal auditory stream but virtually absent in prefrontal cortex. The authors suggest these regions as candidate targets for neuromodulation-based cochlear implant rehabilitation.

papers.title: Tracking Neurophysiological Trajectories in Adolescent Non-Suicidal Self-Injury During Mindfulness-Based Intervention: A Longitudinal Single-Channel EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a prospective longitudinal observational study of 52 hospitalized adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury undergoing home-based EEG biofeedback meditation, exploratory responders showed progressive increases in single-channel alpha/beta ratio that were positively associated with total mood disturbance improvement (r=0.43). The authors conclude that EEG trajectory analysis may be a promising objective monitoring approach, though a control group was lacking.

papers.title: Intranasal dexmedetomidine sedation in pediatric electroencephalography: dose optimization, safety, and EEG characteristics.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 224 children undergoing EEG under intranasal dexmedetomidine sedation, initial sedation success was ~94.6-94.7% with median 10-minute onset and mild self-limited adverse events in ~3%. In a small paired subgroup of 11 patients, no significant spectral power differences from chloral hydrate were detected, but equivalence could not be established.

papers.title: Neural Profiles of Pistol Shooting Performance Across Skill Levels in Hearing and Deaf Shooters: Insights into Cognitive-Motor Processes.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
papers.summary: Examined EEG oscillations during the 4 s preceding trigger pull in skilled versus novice hearing (Study 1) and deaf (Study 2) air-pistol shooters. Skilled hearing shooters showed lower temporal alpha asymmetry and higher posterior, frontocentral, and frontal midline theta power, whereas skilled deaf shooters showed reduced frontocentral alpha and sensorimotor rhythm power, indicating expertise-related neural profiles differ with sensory experience.

papers.title: Data-Driven EEG-fMRI Fusion: From Multimodal Integration to Latent Neural Inference.
papers.summary: Reviews data-driven EEG-fMRI fusion methods published 2000-2025, organizing them by symmetric vs. asymmetric strategies, factorization vs. translation objectives, and linear vs. nonlinear assumptions. Reports that fusion reveals distributed network dynamics inaccessible to unimodal analyses, while noting the absence of a universal validation standard and persistent challenges of temporal misalignment and model-dependent interpretation.

papers.title: A state-of-the-art review of biosensor-based markers for tinnitus.
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates biosensor-based approaches for identifying objective markers of tinnitus, cataloguing electrophysiological, brain imaging, and physiological methods. It concludes that EEG is a promising but currently limited approach, since inconsistent findings and poor reproducibility remain major barriers to clinical translation despite promising AI-based classification.

papers.title: Routine greenery encounters and anxiety occurrence probability: a study of component contributions in university residential greenery scenes based on mobile electroencephalography data.
papers.summary: This exploratory study related mobile EEG-derived Anxiety Occurrence Probability (frontal alpha asymmetry, theta/beta ratio) to 13 quantified greenery components along a 45-m campus route in 35 university students. Color richness, shading rate, green view ratio, and visibility were negatively associated with AOP (model adjusted R² = 0.770), with piecewise breakpoints of 0.321 for shading rate and 0.451 for visibility; findings are correlational.

papers.title: ALI MEA60: A porous thin-film microelectrode array for air-liquid interface electrophysiology of 3D excitable tissues
papers.summary: Developed and characterized the ALI MEA60, a porous polyimide thin-film microelectrode array with 60 electrodes for air-liquid interface electrophysiology of 3D excitable tissues, compatible with a commercial acquisition system. Across 41 devices it showed median impedance of 56 kOhms and ~5 uV saline RMS noise, stable recording for at least 60 days with ~85% channel persistence, expected pharmacological responses in neural spheroids and cardiac organoids, and cross-tissue compatibility.

papers.title: Electrophysiological correlates of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia during the anticipation and delivery of pain
papers.summary: Feasibility study adapting a placebo-nocebo conditioning pain paradigm to EEG in 20 healthy adults, successfully inducing placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia via verbal instructions, conditioning, and sham TENS. Found increased theta, alpha, and beta power in placebo vs. control during pain delivery and in nocebo vs. control during anticipation and delivery, with gamma-band power increased in nocebo vs. placebo as a function of perceived pain intensity.

papers.title: Spreading voltage buildup in high density EEG during migraine aura: A longitudinal single-patient study.
papers.summary: Longitudinal 256-channel high-density EEG in a single patient with migraine with aura detected a spreading voltage buildup with contralateral maximum and spreading delta-band power increase during aura, with an estimated spread velocity of 3.8 mm/min, suggested to reflect cortical spreading depolarization.

papers.title: Changes in negative affect and resting-state EEG power following an EEG-derived generative reality art experience: a pilot pre-post study.
papers.summary: This single-group pilot pre-post study exposed 30 healthy students to a 5-min EEG-derived generative VR art experience and measured affect and resting-state EEG. Negative affect decreased (mean change -3.13) and absolute alpha/beta power decreased in frontal, frontocentral, and central regions, but EEG changes were not associated with affect changes and no neural mechanism or causality was established.

papers.title: Predictors of Anesthetic Augmentation in Electroconvulsive Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort of 527 patients (4,016 propofol-based ECT sessions) identified shorter first-session EEG seizure duration (OR=0.968) and higher first-session stimulation energy (OR=1.044) as independent predictors of anesthetic augmentation, while age was not significant. An exploratory two-predictor risk score achieved AUC=0.786, and all augmentation strategies prolonged seizures with comparable clinical improvement.

papers.title: Validation of drug-resistant epilepsy identification algorithms in US Veterans across diverse care settings.
authors: Veterans Epilepsy Learning, Collaborative Research, and Operations (VELCRO) investigators
papers.summary: This multicenter retrospective validation study evaluated 96 medication- and utilization-based algorithms for identifying drug-resistant epilepsy in 970 US Veterans on ≥2 antiseizure medications, using chart review as reference. The best algorithm (3+ ASMs, or 2 ASMs for ≥1 year, plus EEG/MRI and intractable ICD code documentation) achieved AUC 0.701 overall (0.756 CEC, 0.678 non-CEC), supporting standardized DRE identification in VHA administrative data.

papers.title: [Research on the underlying mechanisms of electroacupuncture in improving colonic dysmotility in ulcerative colitis mice based on cyclic nucleotide-gated cation channels].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.summary: In DSS-induced ulcerative colitis mice, electroacupuncture at ST37 reversed colonic dysmotility, reducing elevated colonic HCN2, 5-HT, TPH1, and SERT expression and normalizing transit time and propulsion rate. Intestinal epithelial HCN2 deletion and RIN-14B knockdown reduced 5-HT and cAMP, supporting HCN2 in enterochromaffin cells and 5-HT release as the mechanism.

papers.title: Influenza A-Associated Encephalitis and Encephalopathy in Adults: An Exploratory Criteria-Based Analysis.
papers.summary: Retrospective exploratory analysis of five adults with PCR-confirmed influenza A and acute neurological symptoms, applying International Encephalitis Consortium 2013 criteria to classify three as encephalitis and two as encephalopathy. The study found the categories overlapped substantially and did not determine treatment, with three patients asymptomatic at 3 months and two with persistent deficits.

papers.title: De novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant presenting with neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia, with favorable response to low-dose dopamine therapy: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a girl with a de novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant causing NEDHIB who presented with neonatal hypotonia, later sleep-associated dystonia-like nodding, and neurodevelopmental regression with loss of walking, sitting, and language. Low-dose levodopa-benserazide produced marked motor and cognitive improvement and complete resolution of nodding episodes.

papers.title: WITHDRAWN: Identifying Phelan-McDermid-Like Electrophysiological Subtypes in Autism Using EEG and Machine Learning
papers.summary: This manuscript was withdrawn by the authors pending re-evaluation of the clinical data, and they request it not be cited; no findings are reported in the available abstract.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
